slides.title:
An acquisition doesn't
join two networks.
slides.body:
It joins two sets of
*assumptions* about who is trusted.

slides.title: And nobody documented either
slides.body: Not in a policy. Not anywhere.

slides.title: What gets scoped first
slides.body:
Address space. Routing between
two cores. DNS resolving both ways.
Real work, *known answers*.

slides.title: The half that overruns
slides.body: Is the part nobody wrote down.

slides.title: In their estate
slides.body:
A flat segment carrying production —
because ten years ago the team was
small and everyone shared a building.

slides.title: In yours
slides.body:
A rule permitting a source range,
for a project that ended in *2021*.

slides.title: Neither is written as a policy
So what do you actually get?
slides.body:
Not the union of two security
postures. The *weaker* one,
applied to everything.

slides.title: Integration is cheap.
slides.body:
Reconciling two undocumented
trust models is *the project*.

Follow *@mzsnetworks*
